reason: The text extensively portrays the Hebrews (Israel) as followers of Yahweh (יְהוָה). The primary narrative depicts God calling Israel into covenant at Mount Sinai, with the people repeatedly affirming their commitment: 'All that Yahweh has spoken we will do' (כֹּל אֲשֶׁר־ דִּבֶּר יְהוָה נַעֲשֶׂה). God establishes them as 'a kingdom of priests and a holy nation' bound to His commandments. Even the golden calf incident, while showing temporary apostasy, is framed as a violation of their covenant relationship with Yahweh—presupposing they are meant to be His followers. Throughout, Israel's identity is defined in relation to Yahweh as their God who redeemed them from Egypt and demands their exclusive devotion.
